questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Labor demand MRP = 60 - 3L and supply W = 6 + L; find monopsony employment.
questions.explanation: With labor supply W = 6 + L, total labor cost is 6L plus L squared, so marginal factor cost is 6 + 2L. Setting MRP equal to marginal factor cost gives 60 minus 3L = 6 + 2L, so 54 = 5L and L = 10.8. Equating MRP with the wage instead gives 13.5, the competitive level rather than the monopsony choice.
questions.hint: A monopsony equates MRP with marginal factor cost, not with the wage.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Explain why a minimum wage can raise employment in monopsony but not in perfect competition.

answer.exemplar: In monopsony a moderate floor can flatten MFC and raise employment, whereas in perfect competition a binding floor raises wage above equilibrium and reduces labor demand.

questions.explanation: A monopsony faces marginal factor cost above the wage, so a moderate minimum wage can flatten that wedge and raise employment. In perfect competition the wage equals marginal factor cost, and a binding floor raises the wage above equilibrium, cutting labour demand.
